leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer B028 as a single-achievement prize, and all four name the same slate: Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, for the Z2 quantum spin Hall prediction plus the first HgTe observation. The citation wording differs slightly (Eriksson, Johansson and Mehlig mention Z2 topological insulators and HgTe quantum wells; the Chair's wording speaks only of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators). Shared ground is the theory-plus-decisive-experiment pattern and two decades of reproduction. Not shared is how comfortable each is with the credit boundary: all four state that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D strand (Hasan, Fu, Moore, Balents, Roy) are left outside, and Mehlig says a slate with Hasan would be at least as defensible. Danielsson also lists B028 as a first alternative, but does not prefer it in the round-1 configuration.

Two members prefer B034 alone, both with Katori and Ye and a citation centred on magic-wavelength optical lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level. They agree that attribution is compact and that reproduction by several laboratories settles maturity. They share the main objection themselves: the 2005 and 2012 prizes may make this look like incremental precision, and Lemonde, Takamoto and Ludlow/Bloom might claim a share. Lindroth also warns that this is her own field and she may overvalue it. Kroll asks what the discovery is beyond capability. Neither has named a concrete finding obtained with the clocks that goes beyond prospects.

Olsson prefers B046 alone with Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald and Bistritzer, having replaced Andrei with Bistritzer after the opening round. Her case is the Bistritzer-MacDonald 2011 prediction followed by the 2018 experiments. She says she would not wait for the pairing mechanism. She still flags Andrei's earlier STM evidence and earlier continuum-model theory by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto as unresolved attribution questions. B046 is also the first alternative of Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Pearce and Kroll, and Olsson reports that all eight members ranked it in the opening. Those alternatives are not counted here as preferred configurations.

Danielsson is the only member whose configuration has two parts: Halzen alone for IceCube, and MacDonald with Jarillo-Herrero for twisted bilayer graphene. His rationale is two distinct discoveries and the three-person ceiling. He concedes that a solo IceCube award invites credit objections (AMANDA, DUMAND, Baikal, the wider collaboration) and that the two-name B046 part omits Bistritzer and Andrei. He says he would not oppose B028 if B005 cannot be defended, and would revert to a Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald, Bistritzer slate if B046 stood alone. B005 is not in anyone else's round-1 configuration, although the Chair ranked it first in the opening and lists it as an alternative.

areas_of_agreement: No round-1 member objects to the reality or reproducibility of the science behind B028, B034 or B046; disagreement is about novelty, credit and maturity, not about whether the effects exist.

Four of eight members prefer B028 with the same three names (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp), and the other four preferred configurations (B034, B046, B005+B046) each name two to three people within the three-person limit.

B046 is the most common first alternative: Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Pearce and Kroll list it second, and Danielsson includes it in his own configuration. B034 is the next most common alternative (Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson). These are not counted as preferred positions.
Several members state the same attribution problem for B028: the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe prediction and the 3D strand through Hasan are outside the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio.

Members agree that the prize should be for the discovery and not for a final explanation, which matters for the open pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene (explicit in Olsson's statement, implicit in Danielsson's).
scientific_disputes: Whether B028 is a distinct achievement or too close to the 2016 topological-phase prize: Eriksson, Mehlig and Johansson say it extends but does not duplicate; Danielsson asks what the prize adds that 2016 did not, and the Chair and Mehlig list it as an open concern.

Whether B028 should cover only the 2D quantum spin Hall effect or topological insulators as a class including the 3D strand; Mehlig notes the HgTe edge conductance fell short of perfect quantisation and that a sceptic might call the experimental half thin.

Whether B034 is a new conceptual step or a precision refinement of the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and whether the new observables (redshift over millimetres, constants, dark matter, geodesy) are results or prospects (Kroll's own question, Danielsson's challenge).

Whether a detector-driven discovery with an unexpected answer from nature (B005) should outrank the stronger committee-wide support for B028 and B046, a question raised by Danielsson and the Chair, with the Chair stating that condensed matter is outside his expertise.
attribution_disputes: B028: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe prediction) and Hasan, Fu, Moore, Balents and Roy (3D) are outside the Kane, Mele, Molenkamp slate. Mehlig asks whether Hasan should replace Mele or Molenkamp. B028 as listed credits four names, so the committee must choose among them; Hasan is the one listed name left out of the proposed trio.

B046: Olsson names Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald and Bistritzer; Danielsson names only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero because of the three-person ceiling. Andrei (earlier STM evidence from 2010) is listed in the ballot but in no member's slate, and Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto (earlier continuum-model theory), Cao and Fatemi (2018 bench work) are raised by Olsson and not in the ballot.
B005: only Halzen is credited, so the claims of AMANDA, DUMAND, Baikal and the IceCube collaboration cannot be tested from the supplied names; Danielsson and the Chair both say this.
B034: Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Bloom and ion-clock groups may have partial claims against a Katori and Ye slate (Kroll, Lindroth).
Danielsson's two-part configuration spreads three seats over two achievements, which forces a choice inside B046 that Olsson's single-part version does not.
maturity_disputes: B046: the 2018 discovery is about eight years old and the superconducting pairing mechanism is still debated (Danielsson, Olsson, Johansson, Eriksson, Pearce); Olsson would not wait for the mechanism, while the Chair and Johansson defer to the condensed-matter judgement.
B034: Kroll asks whether the committee should wait for the redefinition of the second, which has not happened; reproduction across several groups is not disputed.

B028: about two decades of reproduction are not disputed, but Mehlig and Eriksson note modest practical applications, and Danielsson asks whether a second topological prize soon after 2016 is overdue or premature.
B005: Danielsson cites confirmation in several channels and associations with TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane. These are his own recollections, which he flags as unverified.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology; Chalmers hosted Martinis and Clarke as guest researchers) proposes to recuse himself from any decision on B035. B035 is not in any member's round-1 preferred configuration, but is on the shortlist and could re-enter.

Lindroth is a long-time close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and in the same AMO community as the clock and ultracold-atom candidates; she flags closeness for B011 and B034, and notes B034 is her own field and she may overvalue it. She names no collaboration with Katori or Ye.

Kroll spent a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during his PhD (Hall is a 2005 laureate; Kroll describes Ye as a JILA colleague of Hall's lineage), has no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye, and notes that his WACQT leadership overlaps institutionally with Chalmers (B035, not in his configuration).
Olsson is a Fellow of the University of Tokyo (since 2025) and Katori (B034) is Tokyo-based; she reports no direct collaboration with him and no co-authorship with any credited name.
Pearce (the Chair) works in astroparticle fields neighbouring B005 (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, XL-Calibur) but is not in IceCube; he states this is familiarity, not a conflict requiring recusal.

Eriksson notes that, as a theorist computing band structures, he may favour candidates where theory and spectra agree. Mehlig notes only that Johansson and Olsson share the Gothenburg environment. Danielsson reports no conflict.
No member reports a specific personal or institutional connection to any person credited on B028, B046 or B005.
questions_for_round2: B028 members: should the citation cover the 2D quantum spin Hall effect only, or topological insulators as a class? If a class, who should be the third name, and should Hasan replace Mele or Molenkamp? If the 2D only, how should the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang be handled?
Is B028 sufficiently distinct from the 2016 topological-phase prize? What would the citation say that 2016 did not?

For B046: is the unresolved pairing mechanism and an eight-year-old discovery grounds for waiting, or is the existence of the correlated phases enough? Who holds the third seat among Bistritzer, Andrei and others, and what weight does Andrei's earlier STM work carry?

For B034: can Kroll and Lindroth identify a concrete finding obtained with lattice clocks that nature did not allow us to guess, and how does the committee answer the incremental-precision objection against 2005 and 2012? Do the Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Bloom claims alter a two-name slate?

For B005: can a one-person IceCube prize be defended against AMANDA, DUMAND, Baikal and collaboration-scale credit, and does any member see an acceptable name beyond Halzen? If not, does Danielsson's two-part configuration fall to B046 alone or to B028?

Should the committee prefer a single achievement with three names or a two-part prize? Danielsson alone proposes two parts; what would Olsson and the B028 members need to see before supporting a two-part configuration?
Do the conflict disclosures (Johansson on B035, Lindroth on B011 and B034, Kroll and Olsson on B034) require recusal or any other handling at final ballot?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows one position with four explicit supporters (B028, Kane, Mele, Molenkamp), one with two (B034, Katori, Ye), and two single-supporter positions (B046 alone; B005 with B046). No position has a majority, and the four B028 supporters each name credit gaps. B046 is the most widely named alternative but has only two members who put it in their preferred configuration. Disagreement is mostly about attribution, distinctiveness from earlier prizes and maturity. Round 2 should settle those before any position is treated as leading.
